newsitem.title: ITALY: Boat packed with 571 Albanians reaches Italy.
newsitem.headline: Boat packed with 571 Albanians reaches Italy.

text.p: A heavily listing boat built to carry fewer than 50 people limped into a southern Italian port on Sunday crammed with 571 Albanians, coastguards said.
The Albanian vessel was escorted into the port of Barletta on Italy's southern Adriatic coast by coastguard vessels after sending out a distress call.
"The sanitary conditions were appalling," a coastguard office spokesman said by telephone from Barletta. "Even 50 people would have been too many to have on board."

The number was by far the largest on a single vessel to reach Italy from Albania this month following a relative lull after some 13,000 people arrived in March on decrepit boats to escape their country's slide into anarchy.

Initial estimates had said more than 100 people were on board but coastguards said a count had shown the vessel, a fishing boat converted for use as a coastal ferry, was carrying 362 men, 135 children and 74 women, some of them pregnant.
They said the boat had taken 26 hours to cross the Adriatic from a beach near the northern Albanian town of Shokder.

Most of the March arrivals had come from the ports of Durres and Vlore, where an Italian-led multinational military force has since deployed to assist in the delivery of relief supplies to the Balkan state.
Italian customs police meanwhile said they had seized 638 kg (1,400 pounds) of marijuana from an Albanian motor boat that landed near Santa Maria di Leuca on the southern Adriatic coast.

Saturday's find brought the amount of marijuana seized in 10 days along the coast near Lecce, southern Italy, to almost 1.6 tonnes, police said. The haul was the biggest on record in the area and the boat's crew was arrested, they said.

Albania has rapidly emerged as a prime location for the cultivation and smuggling of marijuana. The drugs are usually brought to Italy on motorboats and motorised dinghies that cross the narrow Strait of Otranto with illegal immigrants.
